Theme

Town, shops & places · Money, work & business

cheap adjective

also dirt cheap, as cheap as dirt, inexpensive

classical

Traupman 130
Traupman 289
Traupman 332

vīlis, vīle

Other words

  • prō lutō (esse) — dirt cheap

    also used · classical · Petr. 44: prō lutō erat annōna (Lewis & Short s.v. lutum); Traupman 96; Traupman 289; Traupman 304

    (vōx sermōnis vulgāris: Petr.)

    Literally “(going) for mud”.

Examples

  • «Bene ēmistī,» inquit avus. «Hōc annī tempore vīlia sunt māla.»

    “That’s a bargain,” said Grandpa. “Apples are cheap at this time of year.”Libellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

See also expensive, cost a lot, bargain, get a bargain.

SourcesLewis & Short: vilis
